However, the sausage didn't taste handmade; it felt more like a store-bought product. It was also a bit tough. Next, I tried the Cuốn Diếp Tôm Tươi (lettuce fresh rolls with prawn). The ingredients were fresh, and I enjoyed the dipping sauce that came with it. The rolls were visually appealing, but they fell apart easily when eaten. Lastly, I had the Tàu Hủ Nước Đường Gừng (bean curd in ginger syrup). The tofu was silky smooth texture. The syrup wasn't very sweet, and I could still taste a hint of ginger.

Superb quality, creative and healthy
Apr 2018 • Family
Definitely a place to visit, worth a drive outside the center. The restaurant itself is beautifully decorated and has many seating options, inside and outside. Plants, lanterns wind chimes and soft lighting makes it an ideal place for dinner, in a large company or simply a romantic one. The Spice Bistro is connected to the Hum restaurant and we were offered both menus. The Hum is a vegetarian restaurant, whereas Spice Bistro offers sophisticated street-food, a mixture of Thai and Vietnamese cuisines. It took us quite a while to choose from the extensive list, but as we were 3, we managed to create a menu that samples various dishes. A papaya salad with Anchovies, braised figs in green curry sauce (delicious and without coconut milk), stir fried spinach, lotus leaves filled with whole grain rice and lotus seeds, spicy seafood soup (a great version of a tom yum kung) and excellent fresh fruit sodas. The service was very attentive, even staff that had difficulties with English tried their best. We will for sure be back to try many other delicious and interesting dishes, that can hardly be found elsewhere. 
In addition, prices are very fair and you can be sure to get top quality for what you pay.
